subject: Proposal: annual prepay conversion with tiered discount & ramp safeguards
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@opswing.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@opswing.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: annual prepay conversion with tiered discount & ramp safeguards

Hi Jamie / Opswing procurement team,

Great speaking with you on Friday — thanks for the transparency about usage variability during your Q1 product launch. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a compact proposal on the table for moving from monthly invoicing to an annual prepay (covering inference + embeddings traffic) that balances meaningful term discounts with ramp protections so you don’t pay for capacity you aren’t yet using.

High-level proposal (summary attached):
- Term options: 1-year prepay (annual invoice) or 2-year prepay (annual invoice each year)
- Discounts: 15% off list for 1-year, 22% off list for 2-year (applies to committed token/embedding units)
- Ramp protection: Q1 true-up only; if actual usage < 60% of committed in Q1, Opswing receives a one-time onboarding credit equal to 15% of the shortfall invoice amount (applied to next invoice)
- Step-up growth: monthly true-ups allowed; if usage exceeds commit, overages billed at a discounted overage rate (10% above committed unit price)
- Step-down guardrails: contract allows a one-time 10% downward adjustment at 12-month anniversary with 60 days notice (to prevent over-commit uncertainty)
- Migration assistance: one-time onboarding credit of $25k (service credits) for data-migration & integration runbooks

Attached is a concise proposal PDF and a billing worksheet so your finance team can model the cashflow. If this direction looks promising, we can have Karthik and Ben propose final pricing language and Laura loop in finance for invoice cadence.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm target term (1yr vs 2yr) and whether Opswing requires quarterly invoicing inside the annual prepay (we can accommodate but it affects discount level)
2) Legal to send MAAP redline items you care about — we can accept a narrow set of modifications for billing/term language
3) If agreed, I’ll route a final proposal for signature (DocuSign) and we’ll schedule an onboarding kickoff the week after signature

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: annual prepay conversion with tiered discount & ramp safeguards

Marissa,

Appreciate the clear summary and the worksheet — this is exactly the level Opswing procurement needed to start modeling. A couple quick questions from finance/legal:

1) Will the 15% / 22% discounts be applied to list per-token pricing or net of any custom overage pricing we negotiate?
2) For the Q1 true-up protection, is the onboarding credit refundable cash or a credit against future Redwood invoices? Opswing prefers credits applied to invoices rather than refunds.
3) Can we get a simple example of how the one-time 10% downward adjustment would work operationally if we exercised it at the 12-month mark?

We’ll also need a standard SOC-2 addendum and a short runbook for SR/uptime SLAs attached to the MAAP. If you can route the DocuSign-ready contract with the anticipated schedule and invoice milestones that will help us move quickly.

Cheers,

Jamie Ortiz
Head of Ops & Product, Opswing AI

Team — forwarding Opswing’s questions. Quick internal pricing/ops call notes below and a proposed revision to share back.

Proposed answers/edits:
- Discount basis: applied to our published unit prices (i.e., list), overage pricing will be a defined discounted overage SKU (we should call it "committed overage" at +10% of the committed unit price).
- Onboarding credit: ops prefer credits vs cash. We should lock it as a credit applied to invoices within 12 months (non-refundable).
- Downward adjustment: allow a single 10% reduction to committed quantity at 12-month anniversary with 60-day notice; any reduction creates a proportional reduction in committed spend and discount tiers re-evaluated on next anniversary (this prevents gaming but is customer-friendly).

Numbers I recommend we offer back to Opswing (to keep it competitive but preserve economics):
- 1yr prepay: 14% discount; onboarding credit $25k; Q1 protection threshold 60% with credit equal to 15% of shortfall invoice amount (applied as invoice credit)
- 2yr prepay: 20% discount (year-1 invoice same discount; year-2 reprice at then-current list with a floor), onboarding credit $35k; same Q1 protection but cap total credits at $75k over life

Operational asks: Laura — can finance commit to annual invoice with the option for Opswing to request quarterly invoicing within the prepay (we’d need to move them to annual discounts minus 2% if they want quarterly billing)? Ben — any legal flags on the downward adjustment language? Karthik — can you confirm we can support the "committed overage" SKU in our billing engine and how to show it in invoices?

If we’re aligned I’ll respond to Jamie with the revised bullets and attach the updated worksheet.

—Marissa

Marissa / team,

Legal is okay with the one-time 10% downward adjustment as long as we: 1) include a clause that any downward adjustment cannot reduce committed spend below a 12-month minimum APR-equivalent floor (we usually express this as a 50% committed floor relative to initial commit); and 2) disallow multiple downward adjustments (single-use only).

Finance (Laura) — noted that quarterly invoicing within an annual prepay complicates revenue recognition and reduces the discount. I support the suggestion to price quarterly-invoice option at an effective ~2% penalty to the discount.

Karthik — pls confirm the billing engine will create a distinct 'committed overage' line item with clear unit pricing; Opswing will want that visible on invoices. Also confirm we can cap the total credits to $75k for a 2yr term.

Ben

—

Jamie — thanks for the quick review and for flagging SOC-2 and SLA items. Per internal alignment, here’s the updated position we’d like to send you formally (I’ve attached the revised proposal and a one-page examples worksheet):

Revised commercial summary for Opswing (final draft):
- 1-year annual prepay: 14% discount off list, annual invoice at signature; onboarding credit $25,000 (invoice credit, non-refundable, applied within 12 months)
- 2-year annual prepay: 20% discount off list for year 1; year 2 will be re-evaluated and priced at no lower than 12% discount (floor) based on year-1 consumption; onboarding credit $35,000, total credits capped at $75,000
- Q1 ramp protection: if Opswing’s actual usage in the first 90 days is <60% of committed capacity, Redwood issues a one-time invoice credit equal to 15% of the shortfall amount (applied to next invoice)
- Downward adjustment: single, one-time 10% downward adjustment allowed at month 12 with 60-day notice; committed spend floor = 50% of original committed spend to protect economics
- Quarterly invoicing option: allowed, reduces effective discount by 2 percentage points
- Overages: billed at "committed overage" SKU priced at 110% of the committed unit price (visible as a separate invoice line item)
- Compliance & SLA: SOC-2 addendum included; 99.9% uptime target with credits for sustained breaches (details in MAAP)

Next steps: I can route the DocuSign contract tonight (HubSpot deal updated — link below). If legal has no further redlines, Procurement pick a signing contact and we’ll target an onboarding kickoff the week of Oct 12.
